video.title: Unexpected Discoveries That Confirm The Bible
video.description:
Archaeologists have found ancient cities, writings and objects connected to people and places mentioned in the Bible.

In this video, we look at some of the most fascinating discoveries, including the boat-shaped formation near Mount Ararat, an Assyrian message found in Jerusalem, the Pool of Siloam and the Dead Sea Scrolls.

Some discoveries provide strong evidence, while others are still being studied. But together, they give us a closer look at the real places, people and events behind the Bible.

Watch until the end and tell me which discovery surprised you the most.

#Bible #BibleHistory #BiblicalArchaeology #BibleDiscoveries #Archaeology #Christianity #ChristianFaith #DeadSeaScrolls #NoahsArk #Jesus #OwenBible

transcript.text: structures in the Jordan Valley.
When archaeologists dug at these sites,
they found large open spaces,
pieces of ancient pottery,
and animal bones.
Zertal believed these were places where the ancient Israelites gathered for worship and religious ceremonies.
But why were they shaped like feet?
He believed the answer was connected to a promise God made to Joshua.
In Joshua 1:3, God told Joshua that every place the Israelites set their feet would be given to them.
God made this promise before the Israelites entered the land of Canaan.
Zertal believed the Israelites built these giant stone feet to show that they had taken possession of the land God promised them.
He also believed these structures might have been places called Gilgal in the Bible.
In Joshua 4:19, the Bible tells us that the Israelites camped at a place called Gilgal after crossing the Jordan River.
Zertal suggested that the giant foot-shaped structures were similar gathering places.
Although the exact Gilgal where Joshua camped has not been identified,
today these giant foot-shaped stone walls can still be seen in the Jordan Valley.
The Assyrian message.
In 2025, archaeologists in Jerusalem found an Assyrian message asking Judah about a delayed payment.
This is interesting because the Bible tells us about a similar payment.
About 2,700 years ago, Assyria was one of the strongest kingdoms in the world.
The Bible says King Hezekiah of Judah stopped serving the Assyrian king.
Because of this, King Sennacherib attacked many cities in Judah.
Second Kings chapter 18 says Hezekiah later agreed to give Sennacherib a large amount of silver and gold.
This kind of payment was called tribute.
It was money or valuable goods that a weaker kingdom gave to a stronger kingdom.
Now, fast forward to 2025.
Near the Western Wall in Jerusalem, archaeologists found a tiny piece of clay with Assyrian writing on it.
It was only about 2.5 cm wide, close to the size of a large coin.
Researchers believed the clay was part of a seal used to close an important letter sent to the king of Judah.
But the message on it was very important.
The writing was in Akkadian, the language used by the Assyrians.
The message spoke about a payment that was late.
It also gave a deadline.
The payment had to arrive by the first day of the month of Ave.
Scientists tested the clay and found that it was not made in Jerusalem.
It came from the area where the main Assyrian cities were located.
This means the message may have traveled all the way from Assyria to Jerusalem.
This connection is very interesting.
This small clay message gives us more proof that the Bible was telling the truth about what happened between Judah and Assyria.
The Lachish stone carvings.
In the 1840s, a British man named Austen Henry Layard was digging at an old palace in Iraq when he found something unusual.
On the walls of the palace were large stones with pictures carved into them.
The pictures showed soldiers attacking a city.
Some were using large ramps to reach the top of the city walls, while others were taking people away as prisoners.

beats.content: Archaeologists found large foot-shaped open structures in the Jordan Valley, believed to be ancient Israelite gathering places.
The foot shape is connected to God's promise in Joshua 1:3 that every place they tread will be given to them.
These giant stone feet likely represent Gilgal, where the Israelites camped after crossing the Jordan River.
A new discovery in 2025 of an Assyrian message asking Judah about a delayed payment mirrors biblical accounts.
Historical context of Assyria's dominance, King Hezekiah's rebellion, and the tribute paid as recorded in 2 Kings 18.
Archaeologists in Jerusalem discovered a tiny clay seal impression with Assyrian writing regarding a payment deadline.
Scientific testing proved the clay came from Assyria, confirming direct correspondence and validating biblical history.
In the 1840s, palace walls in Iraq were discovered with stone carvings depicting the Assyrian attack on Lachish.
